scope: Fifty-two statements in seven groups: on a periodic grid the wall never changes the total and only takes motion away as heat; a one-way push changes the total by exactly the push's total; two sides joined by a wall of thickness k meet at a fixed average, with the difference fading as exp(-(2k)t) and the motion lost equal to the heat made; the tanh dip is bounded below by -ε/(2e), so a large enough base viscosity stays nonnegative; a delayed baseline cannot pile up the record, while a frozen baseline only fills; the mentor and student clocks meet at whole prime ticks, and closing the gap at the tick 23 freeze keeps the shared total and gives off a nonnegative 2/25 of the squared gap; the clay drag -K g χ u takes K g χ u² as heat, brakes a box moving together toward the settling speed -σ Σ a / (K Σ g χ), and the integrity step stays between 0 and 1.
open_items: No proof of the three-dimensional Navier–Stokes prize problem, of blowup, or of global regularity.
These are identities on a periodic finite grid and exact one-dimensional or box-averaged models, not a construction of a smooth three-dimensional solution or a singularity.
No proof of the coupled Hug solver, threshold switching, or residual energy balance for the full system.
The clay wall and its yield and recovery step are the model's drag and integrity rules; they are not derived from the Navier–Stokes equations.
No claim that a numerical run's take-off is a true singularity.
